papers.title: Microstructure and Fatigue Damage of 316L Stainless Steel Manufactured by Selective Laser Melting (SLM)
papers.abstract: In this paper, 316L stainless steel powder was processed and formed by selective laser melting (SLM). The microstructure of the sample was studied using an optical microscope, and the fatigue failure of the sample and the characteristics of crack initiation and propagation were analyzed, providing a research basis for the application of SLM-316L. Due to the influence of microstructure and SLM process defects, the fatigue cracks of SLM-316L mainly emerged due to defects such as lack of fusion and pores, while the cracks of rolled 316L initiated at the inclusions near the surface of the specimen. After fatigue microcrack initiation of the SLM-316L specimen, due to the existence of shear stress and tear stress, the crack tip was passivated and Z-shaped propagation was formed. The existence of internal defects in SLM-316L made the microcrack initiation random and diverse. At the same time, the existence of defects affected the crack propagation in the form of bending, bifurcation and bridge, which made the main crack propagation deviate from the maximum load direction.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了SLM 316L不锈钢的疲劳损伤机制，其疲劳分析方法可迁移至生物医用植入物的力学性能评估，但未涉及多孔结构或应力遮挡。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not link porous structure to stress shielding or stiffness matching, lacks biomedical context, and does not report surface roughness or osseointegration relevant to implant applications.

summary_zh.motivation: 分析SLM 316L不锈钢的疲劳损伤行为，为其应用提供依据
summary_zh.method: 通过光学显微镜观察微观组织，进行疲劳试验并分析裂纹萌生与扩展
summary_zh.result: 疲劳裂纹主要源于熔合不良和气孔缺陷，裂纹呈Z形扩展
summary_zh.validation: 通过疲劳实验和微观表征验证了裂纹萌生与扩展机制

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the fatigue damage behavior of 316L stainless steel fabricated by selective laser melting (SLM) for potential engineering applications.
summary_en.method: Microstructure was characterized via optical microscopy, and fatigue testing was conducted to analyze crack initiation and propagation mechanisms.
summary_en.result: Fatigue cracks primarily initiated at lack-of-fusion and pore defects, with Z-shaped propagation due to shear and tear stresses.
summary_en.validation: Experimental fatigue tests and microstructural observations validated the defect-driven crack initiation and propagation model.
